summary.text: King of the Mariandyni who received the Argonauts because they had slain his enemy Amycus; Idmon and Tiphys died at his court.

story.text: Hyginus tells how Lycus honoured the heroes for killing Amycus; there Idmon was gored by a boar and Tiphys died of illness, and Ancaeus took the helm.

Hyginus places Tiphys' death among the Mariandyni in Propontis where Lycus was king; Apollodorus and Apollonius likewise name him lord of the Mariandyni when the Argonauts landed — a tribal kingdom on the Propontis shore, not a named polis, mapped as the Mariandyni edge marker.
